AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Heparins are widely used for the prophylaxis/treatment of thromboembolic events. As adverse effects, heparin-induced skin lesions occur frequently (in 7.5-39% of patients). Skin lesions may be the only clinical manifestation of life-threatening immune-mediated heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, but are commonly caused by a delayed-type hypersensitivity response [heparin-induced delayed-type hypersensitivity (HIHS)]. Risk factors have not been prospectively identified.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To identify possible risk factors for heparin-induced skin lesions from three independent clinical trials in a combined analysis.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A pooled analysis from prospective studies was performed, and possible risk factors were included in a multiple logistic regression analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Obesity (body mass index of > 25), prolonged anticoagulant therapy, prior heparin exposure and younger age (< 55 years) were confirmed as independent risk factors for HIHS. The choice of anticoagulant preparation had the greatest influence. On comparison of dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, unfractionated heparin, and nadroparin, the latter was associated with the highest risk of eliciting HIHS (odds ratio of 30.2, 95%CI: 11.7-77.9).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The high risk associated with nadroparin has been validated in controlled trials, and this emphasizes the singularity of each heparin preparation in terms of allergenicity and that individualized anticoagulation is required.
